scientific_interpretation: Groq was perfectly stable across four valid samples yet consistently selected CODE DEFECT where protected adjudication requires REQUIREMENT UNRESOLVED and zero mutation authority. This is a stronger stable-wrong case than EXP-C-001 because accepting the low-entropy conclusion could authorize a production change despite conflicting requirements. Therefore semantic stability must never resolve authoritative ambiguity or weaken the human/requirement gate.
design_consequences: Authoritative requirement ambiguity has precedence over semantic uncertainty signals.
Low entropy must never convert REQUIREMENT UNRESOLVED into CODE/TEST/FIXTURE mutation authority.
EXP-H must continue to route requirement ambiguity directly to HUMAN_REQUIRED regardless of model stability.
Conditional review thresholds must be evaluated after governance overrides, not before them.
Gemini is removed from active EXP-L calibration until provider availability is restored; this is operational routing evidence, not model-quality adjudication.
limitations: This remains a diagnosis-taxonomy semantic proxy rather than arbitrary free-form semantic clustering.
One provider supplied sufficient model samples.
